hits.vignette: A 9-month-old infant has recurrent fasting hypoglycemia and diffuse hyperpigmentation. Serum cortisol is very low and ACTH is markedly elevated. Sodium, potassium, plasma renin activity, and aldosterone are normal. Sequencing of MC2R shows no pathogenic variant, but the infant is homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in MRAP.
hits.tested_construct: MRAP is an accessory protein required for normal trafficking and function of the ACTH receptor MC2R; loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 2 with ACTH resistance and usually preserved mineralocorticoids.

hits.vignette: A 15-year-old boy has progressive dysphagia and recurrent vomiting. Barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus with distal “bird-beak” narrowing. His parents report that he has never produced normal tears when crying. Examination shows hyperpigmentation and decreased ankle reflexes. Morning cortisol is low, ACTH is markedly elevated, and aldosterone is normal.
hits.tested_construct: Triple-A (Allgrove) syndrome is an autosomal-recessive AAAS disorder characterized by alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and often progressive neurologic dysfunction.

hits.vignette: A 12-year-old boy has lifelong anemia, intermittent jaundice, splenomegaly, and increasing serum ferritin despite few transfusions. Bone marrow examination shows erythroid hyperplasia with numerous binucleated erythroblasts. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SEC23B.
hits.tested_construct: SEC23B is a component of the COPII coat that mediates export of newly synthesized proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum toward the Golgi. Biallelic SEC23B defects impair erythroid maturation and protein trafficking/processing, causing congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II with ineffective erythropoiesis and characteristic binucleated erythroblasts.

hits.vignette: A neonate develops intractable watery diarrhea and severe failure to thrive within days of birth. Small-intestinal biopsy shows loss of the apical brush border and intracellular microvillus inclusions in mature enterocytes. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in MYO5B.
hits.tested_construct: MYO5B encodes myosin Vb, an actin-based motor/tether that cooperates with Rab8/Rab11 recycling pathways to deliver and recycle apical cargo in polarized enterocytes. Loss disrupts apical membrane trafficking and brush-border protein localization, causing severe congenital diarrhea and characteristic microvillus inclusions.

hits.vignette: A 10-week-old infant has persistent hyperglycemia and low endogenous insulin secretion without pancreatic agenesis. Genetic testing identifies an activating pathogenic variant in KCNJ11, which encodes the Kir6.2 subunit of the pancreatic beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channel.
hits.tested_construct: Activating KCNJ11 variants reduce ATP inhibition of the Kir6.2-containing beta-cell KATP channel. The channel remains excessively open despite glucose metabolism, maintaining membrane hyperpolarization and suppressing voltage-gated calcium influx and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

hits.vignette: A 6-year-old boy had severe watery diarrhea and malabsorption beginning in the first weeks of life. The diarrhea gradually improved during infancy, but he subsequently developed intense hyperphagia and severe obesity. Laboratory testing now shows a markedly elevated fasting proinsulin-to-insulin ratio. His parents are healthy first cousins. Intestinal biopsy shows enteroendocrine cells but markedly reduced prohormone convertase 1/3 immunoreactivity.
hits.tested_construct: Biallelic PCSK1 loss causes prohormone convertase 1/3 deficiency, with severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea early in life followed by hyperphagia, obesity, and multiple endocrine processing abnormalities including elevated proinsulin.

hits.vignette: A 6-year-old boy has oculocutaneous albinism, recurrent epistaxis, easy bruising, and frequent bacterial respiratory infections. Laboratory studies show neutropenia with a normal platelet count and prolonged bleeding after minor procedures. Electron microscopy of platelets shows absent dense granules. There are no giant cytoplasmic granules in leukocytes.
hits.tested_construct: AP3B1 deficiency causes Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 2, characterized by oculocutaneous albinism, platelet dense-granule dysfunction/bleeding, neutropenia, and recurrent infections.

hits.vignette: A 4-year-old child is evaluated for bowed legs and delayed motor milestones. Several primary incisors were lost without trauma, and the roots remained attached to the shed teeth. Radiographs show rachitic metaphyseal changes. Serum calcium and phosphate are within the expected range, but serum alkaline phosphatase activity is persistently low for age and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is elevated.
hits.tested_construct: Loss of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity from ALPL pathogenic variants prevents normal hydrolysis of extracellular inorganic pyrophosphate. Accumulated pyrophosphate inhibits hydroxyapatite crystal growth and mineralization of bone and teeth.

hits.vignette: A cultured fibroblast has normally synthesized lysosomal acid hydrolases that are correctly targeted to lysosomes. However, lysosomal luminal pH rises from the acidic range toward neutrality, and degradation of endocytosed macromolecules falls markedly. ATP production is normal.
hits.tested_construct: Lysosomes maintain an acidic lumen through vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase), which hydrolyzes ATP to pump protons into the organelle. The low intralysosomal pH is required for optimal activity of many acid hydrolases and for normal lysosomal degradation.
